desc:
When Black invades here, White isn't strong enough for a diagonal play, but White is still strong enough to make some kind of attack. One-space jumps and contact plays are typical in this intermediate situation, and <A:P15> is both. Leaning against Black, White can gain momentum for an attack on the pincer stone. (Page 177.)

If White is not strong at all on the upper side and does not want to get involved in a running fight, White can make the evasive and purely defensive lower attachment at <B:N18>. This is not so much an attempt to link up as a sacrifice to make shape on the outside. (Pages 175 & 177.)

White can make what looks like the opposite exchange by starting with the upper attachment at <C:N16>, but this is more an outright loss than an exchange. (Page 178.)
